chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
There is no amputation upon the thief until he takes the stolen property out of the house.

key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief; the person who commits theft
key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: the stolen property or the act of theft in context
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the house; the place from which the property is stolen
key_terms.قَطْعٌ: amputation; the prescribed hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.يَخْرُجَ: he takes out; he removes the stolen property from its place

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment for theft applied in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding theft: the prescribed hadd punishment is not applied until the stolen property has been removed from the house. It indicates that the completion of the act, in legal terms, depends on the property being taken out from its protected place.
